name: Jack Henry & Associates
description: Jack Henry runs the core computer systems of about 900 community and regional banks and 700 credit unions, and sells add-on software and services to roughly 5,600 more clients that use someone else's core system. Banks pay it recurring fees (hosting, processing, licence and support) and per-transaction fees on card, ACH and real-time payments it handles for them. It sells to small and mid-sized institutions rather than the big banks, which is why its bank-technology rivals are the large processors FIS and Fiserv plus Corelation and Finastra. Revenue grew 7.1 percent in FY2026 and the company has paid a dividend every quarter since fiscal 1991.

businessLines.name: Core
businessLines.how: Banks and credit unions pay recurring processing and hosting fees (on-premise or private cloud) for core account-processing systems, usually under multi-year contracts, plus licence and implementation fees and one-time deconversion fees when they leave.

businessLines.name: Payments
businessLines.how: Fees per transaction and per account on card processing, ACH, bill pay, real-time payments, and remote deposit and other payments products run for financial institutions; volume-driven.

businessLines.name: Complementary
businessLines.how: Recurring subscription, hosting and support fees for add-on software to banks and credit unions (digital banking, fraud and security, lending, imaging, analytics); also sold to institutions that do not use its core.

businessLines.name: Corporate Services (formerly Corporate and Other)
businessLines.how: Hardware, licence and processing revenue not in the three product segments; carries the technology infrastructure costs, so gross profit is negative by design.
